correctness.rationale: Exact module subtraction identifies \(\chi(g)=F(g)(F(g)-3)/2+T_2(g)\) for every \(n\ge4\). Integer sign analysis identifies all negatives as \(-1\) on \(F\in\{1,2\}\) with \(T_2=0\), and character orthogonality plus cycle counting yields the exact \(L^1\) mass. Left-right symmetrization makes the central convolution projector minimal among all projections. The exponential generating function \(e^{-z-z^2/2}/(1-z)\) and a Cauchy estimate give the exact finite formula and limiting constant. A standalone checker enumerates \(4\le n\le8\), validates character orthogonality, and checks forbidden-cycle recurrences to \(m=14\); the infinite assertion is proved separately.

originality.rationale: The evaluated norm of the full regular Specht \(n-2,2\) coefficient block was not found in the inspected source statements and full relevant texts. General character polynomial, harmonic analysis, and canonical central idempotent are credited as old; neither a standard-block norm nor a Johnson-scheme norm implies this distinct absolute-character sum. The novelty is the evaluated sharp minimum projection norm, exact short-cycle probability reduction, and full equality classification; the risk of an older character-\(L^1\) evaluation remains disclosed.
residual_risks: The character polynomial and central projection are classical, and a character-L1 identity in an unindexed monograph or table could make the evaluated number a known corollary.
Searches and article comparisons cannot certify global novelty; third-party bibliographic review is not performed.

value.rationale: The exact natural invariant is the minimum projection norm of the full next-lowest two-row Specht block on \(S_n\). Its all-\(n\) short-cycle formula, exhaustive normer classification, quadratic growth contrast with the standard block, and super-geometric normalized error give substantial, non-arbitrary mathematical information at this representation-theoretic endpoint. No new claim is attached to the classical character polynomial or central idempotent by itself.
